name: Israel asking for a king
charge: Rejecting the Lord, that he should not reign over them, to be like all the nations
summary: The elders came to Samuel at Ramah asking for a king to judge them like all the nations. It displeased Samuel, and the Lord told him the people had not rejected the prophet but had rejected Him as their king. Samuel told them the ways of the king who would reign over them, that he would take their sons, their daughters, their fields and a tenth of their grain, and that they would cry out in that day and the Lord would not answer them; and they answered that they would have a king anyway. The ways of the king came to pass under Solomon and Rehoboam, and the door of the covenant was left open to the nation still.
offenseFull: The elders of Israel came to Samuel at Ramah, saying he was old and his sons did not follow his ways, and asked for a king to judge them like all the nations (1 Samuel 8:4-9). Moses had prophesied it: Israel would come into the land and want a king like the nations around them, and the king was to be one the Lord chose, from among their brethren, never a foreigner (Deuteronomy 17:14-15). Moses was shown from the beginning to the end; he saw Israel rejecting the Lord and wrote it down for us to read. Where do we see it today? Voting. We say the same thing when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High, and the answer we hear is that this one is the lesser of two evils, when they are both evil. We reject Him also by keeping their holidays and walking in their ways; we have made a covenant with them.

It displeased Samuel, and he prayed; the Lord told him to listen to the people, for they had not rejected him but had rejected the Lord as their king, as they had done ever since Egypt, forsaking Him for other gods. Joshua had warned us about this at Shechem, where Israel made the covenant with its own mouth and became witnesses against itself that it had chosen the Lord (Joshua 24:21-22). Asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. Christ gave the same picture in the nobleman who went away to receive a kingdom, whose citizens sent word after him that they refused to have him as their king (Luke 19:12-14). The spirit that said set a king over us is the same spirit that says it of Christ.

Samuel told the people what the king would do (1 Samuel 8:11-20). He would take their sons for his chariots and horsemen, to plough his ground, reap his harvest and make his weapons; their daughters as perfumers, cooks and bakers; the best of their fields, vineyards and olive groves for his servants; a tenth of their grain, vineyards and flocks; their servants, their finest young men and their donkeys for his work, and they would be his slaves. And they would cry out in that day because of the king they had chosen, and the Lord would not answer them. The repeated word is take. Still the people refused to listen and insisted on a king, to be like all the nations, with a king to judge them and fight their battles.
judgmentFull: Samuel repeated the people’s words to the Lord, and the Lord told him to give them a king (1 Samuel 8:19-22). He gave them exactly what they asked for. At Mizpeh Samuel set the choice before them once more in the Lord’s words: He had brought Israel out of Egypt and rescued them from every kingdom that oppressed them, and that day they had rejected the God who saved them from all their troubles and demanded a king (1 Samuel 10:18-19). Remember what they had just come out of. Every time one of the judges rose up and delivered us from oppression, we got right during the life of that judge, and when the judge died we went right back into our falling; and now they wanted a man on a throne in place of the God who had done all the delivering.

It all came to pass as Samuel said. Solomon conscripted thirty thousand men from all Israel and sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand, a month there and two months home (1 Kings 5:13-14). Rehoboam made the yoke heavier still, rejecting the counsel of the old men for the young men he grew up with and answering the people harshly (1 Kings 12:13-14). We rejected the Lord and wanted a king like all the other nations, and this is what we got, and look at our condition now, ruler after ruler and nothing getting any better for us. At the wheat harvest Samuel called on the Lord for thunder and rain on a day they expected clear skies, and the people, terrified, begged him to pray for them so they would not die, for they had added to all their sins the evil of asking for a king (1 Samuel 12:14-19). Yet the door was left open. If they would fear the Lord, serve Him, obey His voice and not rebel, both they and their king would continue following the Lord; if not, His hand would be against them as it was against their fathers. A crown did not move Israel outside the covenant. The nation still had to obey the King whose rule it had tried to trade away.

lawsResolved.text: Warnings against an all-powerful leader, king or central government.
The powers of government are appointed by God and are in His hand.
Civil leaders are to be of God.
Do not to follow the ways of other nations.

text.text: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah,
And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.
But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.

According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.
Now therefore hearken unto their voice: howbeit yet protest solemnly unto them, and shew them the manner of the king that shall reign over them.

When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me;

Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the Lord.
And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.
He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.
But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and some shall run before his chariots.

And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties; and will set them to ear his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and instruments of his chariots.
And he will take your daughters to be confectionaries, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.
And he will take your fields, and your vineyards, and your oliveyards, even the best of them, and give them to his servants.
And he will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give to his officers, and to his servants.
And he will take your menservants, and your maidservants, and your goodliest young men, and your asses, and put them to his work.
He will take the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants.
And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you; and the Lord will not hear you in that day.
Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay; but we will have a king over us;
That we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.
Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay; but we will have a king over us;
That we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.
And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord.
And the Lord said to Samuel, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king. And Samuel said unto the men of Israel, Go ye every man unto his city.

And said unto the children of Israel, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you:

And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before the Lord by your tribes, and by your thousands.
And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.
And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses: a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.
And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;

And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

If ye will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God:
But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.
Now therefore stand and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes.

Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.
So Samuel called unto the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.

And ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saved you out of all your adversities and your tribulations; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before the Lord by your tribes, and by your thousands.
